newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer says M3 growth no inflationary threat.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says M3 growth no inflationary threat.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday that although Germany was experiencing strong money supply growth, there was no inflation danger.
He said that M3 growth overstated the levels of liquidity in the economy, but this did not present a threat to price stability.
"M3 has grown more strongly than we had anticipated," Tietmeyer said. "However, money supply growth is still not inappropriate and there is no danger of inflation.
Tietmeyer was speaking at a news conference following a regular policy-setting council meeting.
The Bundesbank chief also said that the current economic situation in Germany gave no reason for a change in policy.
"Both the stronger growth in M3 at the turn of the year, as well as the external value of the mark, count for our steady- hand policy," Tietmeyer said.
